name: Regroup
caption: Your D has the puck at your blue line with time. The forwards had gone ahead and are now swinging back to regroup. Their team has set up a 1-2-2 in the neutral zone.

options.text: Swing back toward my D, low and wide on my side, timing it so I am skating up ice when he is ready to pass.
options.feedback: Right. A regroup is about timing: come back far enough that you receive the puck going forward, with speed, instead of flat-footed at the red line.

options.text: Stop at the red line on my side and wait for the pass.
options.feedback: A stationary target in front of their 1-2-2 is exactly what the trap wants. You would receive it standing still with a winger on you.

options.text: Stretch to their blue line for a long pass over the top.
options.feedback: It can work once as a surprise, but through a 1-2-2 the long pass is usually picked off, and you are offside if it is chipped in. Keep it as the second option.

options.text: Cross over to the left side to confuse them.
options.feedback: Two wingers on one side leaves your D with nobody on the right. Keep your lane; the center is the one who crosses.

questions.prompt: Tap the spot you swing back to before turning up ice.
questions.label: Swing low and wide

fb.right: That is the swing: low enough to receive the pass going forward, wide enough to keep your lane.
fb.close: Close. Come a little deeper; you want to be skating up ice with speed when the pass arrives, not just starting.
fb.wrong: Think timing, not position. Come back low and wide on your side so that you are moving forward when your D is ready.
